question.text: How are capital gains on debt mutual funds purchased after April 1, 2023 taxed?

answer.text: At 20% with indexation benefit if held for more than 3 years
At 10% flat rate regardless of holding period
At the investor's income tax slab rate regardless of holding period
At 12.5% if held for more than 12 months

explanation.text: The Logic: Under amendments introduced by Finance Act, 2023 (effective for investments made on or after 1 April 2023), capital gains on units of specified mutual funds — including debt-oriented schemes that do not invest more than 35% in domestic equity — are deemed short-term irrespective of holding period and taxed at the investor's applicable income-tax slab rate. The earlier benefit of 20% with indexation after 3 years was withdrawn for such purchases. The Trap: "20% with indexation benefit if held for more than 3 years" was the pre-1 April 2023 treatment and no longer applies to new purchases. "10% flat rate regardless of holding period" is not a debt-fund regime. "12.5% if held for more than 12 months" is the LTCG rate for equity-oriented schemes, not debt mutual funds. Note: The cited NISM Series V-B workbook pages (119-120, 125-126) support that Budget 2023 changes apply from 1 April 2023 with the old structure applicable to earlier purchases, but do not explicitly state that debt mutual fund gains for post-April 2023 purchases are taxed at the investor slab rate regardless of holding period. The framing above reflects current Income Tax Act provisions as amended by Finance Act, 2023.
